intro: The fastest way to jump to unread message in Slack on Mac is to click into a conversation that has unreads and press ⌘ J. Slack moves focus to an unread message in that conversation, so you can start reading from there instead of scrolling back through the history.
tldr: Click into a channel or direct message that is bold in the sidebar, then press ⌘ J.
To see unreads across every channel and DM, press ⌘ ⇧ A or click Unreads under Home.
Move between unread conversations with ⌥ ⇧ ↓ for next and ⌥ ⇧ ↑ for previous.
If ⌘ J does nothing, the conversation may have no unreads, or you may be in the web app.
To keep Unreads visible, go to your profile image, choose Preferences, open Home and tick Unreads.

blocks.text: Jump to the first unread message with ⌘ J

Start in the Slack desktop app for Mac. Look at the sidebar under Home. Channels and direct messages with unreads show in bold. Click one so it opens and becomes the active conversation. Then press ⌘ J. Slack moves focus to an unread message in that conversation, so you can read from that point on.

Slack lists ⌘ J as a desktop app shortcut in its keyboard shortcuts article. That matters if you usually work in a browser tab. The Slack pages I checked do not give a web app equivalent. For this shortcut, open the desktop app.
The shortcut only works from inside a conversation. If you press it while the sidebar has focus, nothing moves. Click the message list once, then press the key again.
Test which unread message ⌘ J picks

Two Slack help articles describe this key differently. The keyboard shortcuts article says it jumps to the most recent unread message in a conversation. The navigation article says it moves focus to the first unread message. Those phrases point at different messages, so test it yourself.

Pick a conversation with at least three unread messages. Note the timestamp of the oldest unread and the newest unread. Press ⌘ J and see which message gets focus. Repeat the test once in another conversation to confirm the result.
Slack's notes do not say which behavior each release uses. Trust your own test over any summary, including this one. Once you know which message you land on, you can plan your reading around it.
Open every unread in one list with the Unreads view

Use the Unreads view when you want every unread across channels and direct messages in one place. Press ⌘ ⇧ A, or click Unreads at the top of the sidebar under Home. Slack's help article gives both routes for desktop.

Here is a simple routine. Say you come back from a meeting with unreads in several places. Press ⌘ ⇧ A, then press F6 to move focus into the message list. Use ↑ and ↓ to move between messages. When a group is done, press Esc to mark it read.

Inside Unreads, you can sort the list by sidebar order, alphabetically, by recommended order, by newest activity, or by oldest activity. Pick oldest activity when you want to clear things in the order they arrived. Pick newest activity when the latest thread matters most.

You can also filter by sidebar section. Slack says custom sections need a paid plan. If a conversation seems missing, check the sort and the filter first. A filter you set last week can hide the thing you want today.

blocks.caption: Desktop keys from Slack's Unreads help article

blocks.text: The Unreads view on desktop does not let you send new messages. To reply, click a message's timestamp. That opens the message in its conversation, where you can type. Typing in the list itself does nothing useful, so click through first.
Move between unread channels with the keyboard

Option Shift Down Arrow (⌥ ⇧ ↓) jumps to the next unread channel or direct message. Option Shift Up Arrow (⌥ ⇧ ↑) goes back to the previous one. Slack's shortcut page lists both keys together, so they work as a pair.
A simple routine works well. Press ⌥ ⇧ ↓ to land on the first unread conversation. Read it, press Esc to mark it read, then press ⌥ ⇧ ↓ again. Keep going until nothing is bold in the sidebar.
Use ⌥ ⇧ ↑ when you pass a conversation by mistake. It walks back up the order. You do not have to start over from the top of the list.
Mark messages read, unread, or everything read

Esc marks the messages in the current conversation read, according to Slack's shortcut page. Shift Esc marks every message read. Option-click on a message marks it unread again, so it stays on your list until you deal with it.

Shift Esc is the risky one. It clears unreads across everything, not only the conversation you are in. Slack's Unreads article describes a Mark All Messages Read option at the bottom of the desktop view, with an Undo option. If you hit it by mistake, click Undo right away.
There is also a mouse route for marking a message unread. Hover over the message, click the three dots, and choose Mark unread. Slack's send and read article describes this on desktop.
Use these keys to manage the list, not only to clear it. Marking a message unread is a reminder to yourself. A long thread may need a second read later, so leave it marked.
Pin Unreads to your sidebar

If you keep reaching for Unreads, pin it. Click your profile image, choose Preferences, and open the Home tab. Under Always show in the sidebar, tick Unreads. This path comes from Stanford University IT, which described it for Slack's December 2023 redesign. Slack's own article only says to adjust sidebar preferences, so your labels may differ a little.
Stanford's notes also mention an Unreads only filter at the top of Home. Use it when you want Home to show only the items with unreads. It is a filter, so clear it when you want the full list back.
Pinning matters most if you return to Slack several times a day. A visible Unreads entry saves you a search through the sidebar every time you switch back.
When ⌘ J does nothing: fixes to try first
Most failures come from a few causes. Check them in this order. The first check fixes most cases, so start there.

items: Confirm the conversation has unread messages. ⌘ J has nothing to jump to without them.
Confirm you are in the desktop app. Slack lists ⌘ J as a desktop only shortcut.
Click inside the message list first, so focus is in the conversation.
Test the default key in a plain conversation. A remapped shortcut can conflict with it.

blocks.text: Here is a worked example. You open a channel with two unreads and ⌘ J seems to do nothing. Check the sidebar first. If the name is not bold, there is nothing to find. If it is bold, click the message list and press ⌘ J again.

Slack's Mac release notes say version 4.0.0, released July 15, 2019, fixed customized shortcuts on macOS that sometimes did not work. If you have remapped keys, test ⌘ J in a plain conversation with unreads. If it works there, the remap is the likely cause.

blocks.text: Which Slack for Mac version to expect

The Mac release notes list 4.53.280, dated November 3, 2026, as the newest entry dated before today, November 7, 2026. An entry for 4.53.283 is dated November 9, 2026, which is later than today, so I did not count it. None of the five newest entries mention unreads, shortcuts, the sidebar or Home.

I found no version change to these keys. The shortcut pages do not say which release added them. I did not check which version your Mac runs, so compare your version with the notes before you assume a change.
Why fast unread checks matter on busy days

Slack's surveys point at the same pressure. Its State of Work 2023 study surveyed 18,149 desk workers and executives in nine countries. Many desk workers feel they must reply quickly, even after hours.

Slack's after-hours study covered 10,333 workers across six countries. It found that workers who feel obligated to log on report productivity scores 20% lower. Those surveys did not study unread navigation, so read the numbers as context, not proof that one key fixes anything.
A practical use is to pick two or three set times a day to check Unreads. That beats watching bold names all day. The shortcut is only a faster way to read what you already have.
Common mistakes people make with unreads

items: Pressing ⌘ J with no conversation open. Click into the conversation first.
Treating bold as urgent. Bold means unread, but the message may be old. Check the timestamps.
Using Shift Esc to clear one channel. It clears everything. Use Esc for a single conversation.
Typing a reply in Unreads. On desktop, click a message's timestamp to reply.
Forgetting Option-click. Mark a message unread when you need to come back to it.

blocks.text: Ask Lazur where the Unreads button is
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where the Unreads button is. Lazur sees your screen, draws a circle and a label around it, and answers out loud. You can find it in seconds without hunting through the sidebar.
Ask Lazur to walk you through pinning Unreads. It guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click before it moves on. The clicks stay yours, so you see every step before you make it.
Lazur does not click for you, and it does not operate Slack. It is a voice assistant on your Mac that points, guides and explains what is on your screen.
Related Slack tasks on your Mac

If you need to clear the whole list instead of reading it, see [how to mark all messages as read in Slack on Mac](/how-to/mark-all-messages-as-read-in-slack). To find a specific message from earlier, use [how to search messages in Slack on Mac](/how-to/search-messages-in-slack).
Try the shortcut on one busy channel today. Then open Unreads once and move through it with F6 and the arrow keys. Two short passes like that show you which method suits your day.

faq.question: What is the shortcut to jump to unread message in Slack on Mac?
faq.answer: Click into a conversation that has unreads, then press ⌘ J. Slack moves focus to an unread message in that conversation. Slack lists this as a desktop app shortcut.

faq.question: Does ⌘ J work in the Slack web app?
faq.answer: Slack's keyboard shortcuts page lists ⌘ J as desktop app only. The Slack pages I checked do not give a web app equivalent, so use the desktop app for this key.

faq.question: How do I see all my unread messages on Mac?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ ⇧ A, or click Unreads at the top of the sidebar under Home. The Unreads view lists unread conversations across channels and direct messages.

faq.question: Why is Unreads missing from my Slack sidebar?
faq.answer: Open your profile image, choose Preferences, and go to the Home tab. Under Always show in the sidebar, tick Unreads. Stanford University IT also notes an Unreads only filter at the top of Home.

faq.question: What is the difference between Esc and Shift Esc in Slack?
faq.answer: Esc marks the messages in the current conversation read. Shift Esc marks every message read across Slack. Use Shift Esc with care, because it clears everything.

faq.question: How do I mark a message as unread again on Mac?
faq.answer: Option-click the message. You can also hover over it, click the three dots, and choose Mark unread. Slack's send and read article describes the three dots route on desktop.

faq.question: Which Slack for Mac version changed these shortcuts?
faq.answer: I did not find a version that changed these shortcuts. The Mac release notes list 4.53.280, dated November 3, 2026, as the newest entry dated before today. I did not check which version your Mac runs.

steps.name: Find a conversation with unreads
steps.text: In the sidebar under Home, look for channels or direct messages shown in bold. Slack's send and read article says bold names mean there are unread messages. Pick the one you need to read now.

steps.name: Click into the conversation
steps.text: Click the channel or DM name to open it. The message list appears. Keep the conversation active, because the shortcut works from inside it. Click the message list once so focus sits there.

steps.name: Press ⌘ J to jump to the unread messages
steps.text: Slack moves focus to an unread message in the conversation. Slack's two help articles describe this key differently, so check which message you land on.
steps.tip: If nothing happens, the conversation probably has no unread messages to jump to.

steps.name: Open the Unreads view for everything else
steps.text: Use this when you want unreads from every channel and DM in one list. The Unreads view lists unread conversations across your workspace.

steps.name: Move through the Unreads list
steps.text: Press F6 to move focus to the message list. Then use the up and down arrows to move between messages. Press left or right to expand or collapse a group.

steps.name: Jump between unread channels
steps.text: Option Shift Down Arrow moves to the next unread channel or DM. Option Shift Up Arrow goes back to the previous one.

steps.name: Mark a group as read
steps.text: Press Esc to mark the current group or conversation read. Use Shift Esc only when you want to clear every unread, because it applies to everything.
steps.tip: Shift Esc marks all messages read, so check before you press it.

steps.name: Pin Unreads in the sidebar
steps.text: Open Preferences, go to the Home tab, and under Always show in the sidebar, tick Unreads. Stanford University IT describes this path, so your labels may differ slightly.
steps.tip: If the labels differ, look for the sidebar setting that mentions Unreads.

troubleshooting.problem: Shift Esc marked everything read by accident
troubleshooting.fix: Look at the bottom of the desktop Unreads view for Undo. Slack's Unreads article describes a Mark All Messages Read option with an Undo option, so act quickly.

troubleshooting.fix: Slack lists ⌘ J as desktop only, and its Unreads article covers desktop and mobile. I found no official web app equivalent, so click the conversation in the sidebar instead.
